title: Surface + pressure resorption
topic: External surface and pressure resorption stop when their cause stops; the pulp is not the cause, so no root canal treatment.

claims.claim: Surface resorption: small injury -> shallow lacunae in cementum (schematic cells)
claims.source: Abbott PV, Lin S. Dent Traumatol 2022;38:267-285 (PMID 35605161) - full text, section 6.1

claims.claim: Toy model / schematic: cell size, amount of root loss and timing are exaggerated, not to scale (labelled on every sheet)

caption:
Two root resorptions that stop when the cause stops.

SURFACE: one-off injury, shallow lacunae, new cementum in weeks if no infection. Usually not seen on radiographs. No treatment.
PRESSURE (ortho, impacted tooth, cyst/tumor): active while pressure lasts. Remove it and it arrests, but not instantly or always. Lost root length stays lost.
PULP: not the cause. Root canal treatment only if the pulp is diseased; advanced defects can reach it.

Refs: Lin 2022, Abbott & Lin 2022, Fuss 2003, Dent Traumatol; Patel 2022, Int Endod J; Cheng 2009, AJODO; Falahat 2008, Angle Orthod.
